answer.justification: The inferior thyroid artery lies close to the recurrent laryngeal nerve in the tracheoesophageal groove. Ligating it near the pole risks nerve injury, causing unilateral vocal cord paralysis and hoarseness. Internal laryngeal nerve injury produces sensory loss, not hoarseness. External laryngeal nerve injury relates to the superior thyroid artery. Laryngeal edema typically appears early and resolves.
